text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak discusses with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat suggestions to restart the Israeli-Palestinian peace talks and save the peace process. A Palestinian-Israeli meeting on the level of experts to be held in Cairo with an Egyptian mediator present.
- Egypt to hire a specialised firm to promote 50 flagging public sector firms to international investors.
- Parliament refuses to lift the immunity of Mostafa Saeed, head of the economic committee, after it became clear that the requests to do so were from people who were acting out of spite.
- Mubarak receives telephone call from Saudi Crown Prince Abdullah bin Abdul-Aziz. The call was part of the ongoing discussions of topics which are of bilateral concern.
- Parliament to suspend sessions for the summer.

- Sources close to Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu say his government is looking into the possibility of allowing extremist Jewish rabbis into the al-Aqsa mosque in Jerusalem to perform special rites.
- Parliament committee suggests amending the criminal code to only punish surgeons who transplant human organs without the patient's knowledge.
- Constitutional court rules that a worker can receive a pension from the state eventhough he has another job.
- Oil Minister Hamdi el-Banbi says that firms in the oil sector are not for sale.

- Coastguards find two unidentified bodies floating off the coast of Marsa Matruh. Security sources think they might be part of the crew of the "Samir", a ship that disappeared earlier this year in mysterious circumstances.
